summary: Business provider jobs now expose the stored archetype, origin and recurring schedule id, an ordinary-request deadline based on updated_at, owner-only action flags, and the existing accepted-only address projection.
Ordinary acceptance checks the server deadline after acquiring the existing booking lock; recurring occurrences remain exempt, and decline/refund behavior is unchanged.
Request cards use the server deadline and flags, hide an unsupported zero-visit-fee earnings estimate, and link to booking details.
Next-job actions are family-aware; accepted time-based sessions and proposal OTP/delivery actions open booking details, and proposal confirmed/delivery_pending work is active.
Mutation success requires a refreshed same-booking-id status readback. No appearance flag or money-safety gate was added.

The private PostgreSQL fixture preallocates cleanup keys before setup, restores archetype_flags on failure, attempts every cleanup step, and propagates aggregated cleanup failures. An injected setup abort verifies that partial rows are removed and the original configuration is restored.
implementation.featureOffBehavior: No appearance feature gate was added to owner resolution, cancellation, refunds, settlement, or expiry cleanup; the existing money-safety paths were not modified.
